answers.rule_reading: a name-based rule can find a binding for 169 of 169 residual pairs; 119 of those name exactly one origin (clock 58 / data 61), 42 are ambiguous because the symbol is reused in the same module, 29 are selftest fixtures and 8 carry no date at all

method_limits: the population is E504's residual rows (origin=unresolved) and the members it published without a composing site; both come from its face, never re-derived here

resolution is static and single-repository: a symbol is read in the module that names it, then in the module it is imported from (one import hop per level, depth capped at 8), then in the history blob index

the history arm covers python files reachable from HEAD and absent from the working tree, capped at 2500 blobs, fetched with lazy fetching disabled; a blob that is not present locally is skipped rather than fetched, so a hit of zero is a statement about this clone, not about the remote
the history arm is a snapshot: its counts are published, but the gate cannot re-derive them without re-reading every blob, so it is labelled, not re-derived
a track of 'unknown' means the binding says nothing about the day (a caller-supplied parameter, a name bound nowhere); it is never folded into clock or data
selftest fixtures are labelled by the enclosing function name; a fixture that writes outside a test function would be read as a production site
